label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Sunshine Cillage
reports.comment: quick: Very early season run up to the summit of the Divide chair. You can skin from the parking lot but it’s a bit of an adventure. Snow improves considerably around TeePee town chair which is where we got our best turns of the day. About 45cm with a slightly supportive base so we weren’t punching through. Alpine was different - near the top of the Dive, anything from 15-30cm but less consolidate…

reports.title: Walk up Sunshine
reports.comment: quick: Went for a Walk up to Monarch. Snow is still pretty thin even in the alpine. Every pole strike is to ground and depth is variable up to 30 cm. Wind affect in alpine. We had a nice time walking and enjoying the scenery but generally avoided turns.

reports.title: Storm headwall
reports.comment:
quick: Raining hard and 6 degrees at the highway 7am
Snowing at higher elevation with swirling winds 
Very warm even higher up

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Healy Creek Trail was skiable after the first bridge. Around the pass we found the rain crust on all aspects to be very solid (approx 10cm), covered with 5cm of powder. Stuck to some mellow slopes and enjoyed a few turns on what felt like skiing on an icy groomer with 5cm of powder on top. The ski out was fast and sporty.

reports.title: SSV Twin Cairns and Wawa bowl (Nov 11th report)
reports.comment: quick: Nov 11th report - app is acting up. Skied Twin Cairns N face today, followed by the E aspect and then moved to Wawa bowl E aspect. Snowpack was quite similar to the profile posted by Parks. Quick dig on the N aspect of twin cairns at 2440m had a 15cm crust with facets underneath and unconsolidated snow on top with a bit of SH for a total HS of 60cm. Extremely supportive crust. N aspect skie…

reports.title: Wawa hill
reports.comment: quick: Short tour up the hill above the wawa chair. Around 5-10cm of low density powder above the nov 5th rain crust. Excellent coverage didn’t hit any sharks and weren’t many rocks or hazards visible. Snow felt very stable and supportive. Twin cairns looked pretty bony from the resort but wawa bowl and most mellow slopes around the resort looked great.

reports.title: Rock isle lake area
reports.comment: quick: Toured around rock isle lake and skied the backside of standish and the small zone above the lake aswell as the steeper slopes to the lookers left of the ski area boundary above strawberry chairlift. Crust was prevalent everywhere but 10-15cm of low density snow above it. Crust provided good coverage and didn’t find any sharks. Snow felt very stable but wasn’t binding super well to the nov …

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: 10cm of fresh dry snow on a supportive crust layer at the top of the pass.  About 65cm base.

reports.title: Rock Isle Lake Tour & Bourgeau Ice Photos
reports.comment: avalanche: Point release was observed in the bowl above Bourgeau Left Ice Climb but did not reach the climb. / snowpack: 15cm low density (F) snow overlies a 2-3cm crust followed by 1F density snow to ground.

reports.title: Rock Isle SSV
reports.comment: quick: Best conditions to date this year - boot top and even knee deep at Rock Isle. Skied all chutes and we were popping pillows left and right. HS of 90cm on this N aspect with about 45-50cm over the N crust. Crust was about 8cm and facets underneath. Ski pen on the uptrack was a solid 25cm in most locations. No signs of instabilities noted nor did we encounter any wind slabs although we were at…

reports.title: Wawa ridge
reports.comment: quick: Had an amazing day on wawa ridge. Lots of wind transport occurring up there making for some amazing ski quality and wasn’t showing signs of instability. We skied 2 more mellow safer lines with less wind deposited snow first. And cut a decent sized cornice onto a steep ish slope and didn’t find any instability. We felt confident in the snow and finished with 2 laps on the steeper pitch below…

reports.title: Powder laps at Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Amazing day at healy pass. Multiple laps on the N facing slopes. No significant wind slabs or cornices yet, however the wind was strong all day and was beginning to move the new snow around. We were comfortable skiing steep as well as convex slopes, stability was great. Between 50-70cm unconsolidated powder in some places. A thin crust layer seemed to be bonded directly to the ground in the…

reports.title: Skier triggered avalanche
reports.comment: quick: North facing ridge.  We skied cautiously to mellow terrain and avoided the ridge.  The trigger was low and set it off from East to West.  The entire loaded slope of approx 35 degrees was let go instantly.  Settled into a bench right at the top of tree line.   The layer below was a very firm crust.   Didn’t dig into that layer to observe.   Sunday night had significant wind after a good week…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Following up on Cameron Brodrick's report, we skied Healy Pass on Tuesday. Weather was really warm, probably around 5-8° in the mid afternoon.
In the pass the snowpack was roughly 40cm of base snow, 10cm ice crust, 60cm snow on top where I dug my pit. Just over 1m of snowpack. In the photos there is one where my shovel hit the ice crust, and two where I hit the dirt. I'm not professional so…

reports.title: Healy pass
reports.comment:
quick: Skied upto Healy pass area. 
15cm of fresh snow on the trail overnight. 
Warm temps with plenty of trees dropping snow bombs

Skied a lap on a westerly aspect that had heavy sticky snow and was effected from the sun / avalanche: Observed a 1.5 loose avalanche from the previous 12hrs. 

Started under a cornice feature but no evidence to suggest the cornice had triggered it (cornice intact)

reports.comment: snowpack: Snow profile from the Goats Eye snow study plot at Sunshine Village - Parks Canada Visitor Safety

reports.title: bourgeau lake
reports.comment: quick: some small (30cm) cracking was noticed when skinning around the lake, powder on the skin track had all blown away in the alpine. significant wind affect, snow depth on a NW slope varied from 03 to 50cm. moderately stiff, yet light crust was easy to punch through, still plenty of fun to ski. some surface hoar was beginning to form. / snowpack: a few (<1) debris noted just underneath the rock…

reports.title: Healy - Center peak / alpine
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up part of Healy creek then took Marcus’s Y drainage adventure. Popped out of treeline and snow was still unconsolidated. Quickly became more dense and wind pressed just a bit higher up.

Profile at 2314m on E aspect had HS of 85cm on a 35 deg wind loaded slope. Fist to 4F to 1F above the 8cm Cr. Facetting above for about 2cm and below Cr to ground.

CT12 SP down 38cm - ECTP12 down 3…

reports.title: Wawa ridge
reports.comment: quick: Skinned up to the ridge and dug extended column. Broke on 21 on Biden crust. Did not propagate. Severe wind loading as to be expected.

reports.title: Simpson Pass
reports.comment: quick: Skied up Healy Creek and then turned off to ski up to Simpson Pass.  Broke trail in 20cm of light powder once we left Healy Creek Trail.  No signs of instability.

reports.title: Bourgeau Left
reports.comment:
quick: Climbed Bourgeau Left today. Generally good conditions on the climb - some snice in sections especially on the crux last pitch made for a particularly challenging lead. Wind slabs were well formed both above and below the route, but didn't appear inclined to propagate just yet. Still worth keeping an eye on. 

On the drive home, noted several point release slides on N aspects of Mt Rundle, …

reports.title: Twin Cairns - South Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Toured up as far as we could before it was too rocky. Wind affected up top but skied great lower down. Still lots of tracks to be had despite the lack of snow this week.

reports.title: Bourgeau Valley
reports.comment: quick: 75cm snow depth at treeline. 10cm powder on previous surface layer. Temp rise -9 at parking lot to +4 at treeline.

reports.title: Sunny Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Did a fitness skin up to Healy Pass today. Temp was -14 at the start moving to around -5 at the top. Strong inversion present during first half of day. On way up noticed large surface hoar crystals in large clearings/ avalanche run outs up to 3cm. Seemed isolated to bigger clearings around 1900-2000m. SH not present at clearing near top of pass/ tree line. Temperature appeased to be stable …

reports.title: Spray River Falls approach
reports.comment: quick: Approached Spray River Falls this morning but turned around due to poor travel conditions and uncertainty about loading above the climb due to last night’s storm. Very slushy snow, with standing pools of water on the trail in. / weather: Sky was obscured on whole approach, clearing to overcast when back at car park. Winds C to L from the N/NW. Precip Nil to S-1. Temperature hovered around 0…

reports.title: Quartz 2 (Sunshine)
reports.comment: quick: Toured up to Quartz 2 in the Sunshine b-country. Very good early season conditions. Some thin spots on the way up Quartz 1 but easily workable. From the col, we skinned and boot packed our way to the summit of Quartz 2. No signs of instabilities noted during the day.  HS was about 110cm near the ridge. Surface was a combo of HS and facetted snow. We skied the steep convex role (probably som…

reports.title: Harvey Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Encountered rugged travel between the lowest tarn at Harvey Pass down to Bourgeau Lake.

Some walking was required and two wind loaded slopes were crossed. The slopes did not react, but weren't confidence inspiring.

There was evidence of a snowshoer swimming up/across these slopes, which didn't look fun at all.

The descent down the Bourgeau Lake trail was better than expected, though we o…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Snow pit 300 M south of Healy Pass Trail below the ridge, east aspect, 2300 metres, 32º slope.  HS 125 cm	HSS 25 cm
CTH SP 22. 80cm on sun/wind crust 
Also had SP shear on facets; on Nov 5 rain crust at 50cm after prying with shovel.
Snowpack quite unreactive in spite of 2 prominent sliding surfaces. Storm snow powder light and dry. There was about 2 cm fresh overnight.

reports.title: Shooting cracks and windslab development at treeline
reports.comment: quick: We observed shooting cracks consistently near small convexities at tree line. The were significant amounts (40-60cm) of new and wind-transported snow in the zone from the past couple of days. It was snowing lightly throughout our time out there. We skied supported and low-angle terrain. Between our first small lap in this zone at 12:45pm and our our last at 2:15, the upper 5-10cm of the sno…

reports.title: Bourgeau falls
reports.comment: quick: Taken from sunshine gondy of bourgeau falls

reports.title: Bourgeau
reports.comment: avalanche: Pic 1 showing originating high in the alpine, ran over bourgeau falls almost to valley bottom. High winds likely a factor.

reports.title: Surface hoar on East aspect Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Very sensitive snow pack in open trees on East aspect. Observed shooting cracks, with propagation upto 3m from skier and large settling. Quick hand pit showed about 30cm of storm snow on top of surface hoar. Turned around and skied very mellow slopes. A small 0.5 slab avalanche released on a small convexity. 
South facing aspects with heavy wind affect did not have the surface hoar layer.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Several small whumpfs felt while breaking trail on flat terrain between the Wawa lift and Wawa Ridge.  Got a 3-4m shooting crack on the very mellow slope we dropped into.
Significant wind affect and wind transport up in the alpine and treeline.

reports.title: Bourgeau Left
reports.comment: avalanche: Witnessed the end of a loose dry avalanche off Bourgeau Left. 20-25cm of snow fell overnight with a south wind.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Went up on Wawa today to dig and see what's happening. Heavy wind loading on South facing slope. Noted non-propagating cracks while skinning up.

Column test showed:
CTE 8 RP @ 30cm
CTH 6 SP @ 75cm slid like a greased scotchman. Scary stuff.

reports.title: Lower Twin Cairns
reports.comment: avalanche: Naturally triggered avalanche viewable from Mount Standish

reports.title: Sunshine road avalanche control
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche in Bourgeau 4. We also got good results in Bourgeau 7 and across the valley on north facing Eagle 3.

reports.comment: snowpack: ECT, SP.mod14.@50cm .HS130.

reports.title: Ice - Bearspirit
reports.comment:
quick: Approach:
Good bootpack and the ice steps after the cave are fairly easily negotiated.
Only thing some may be unaware of is that the 1a is closed so you cant get to the Fireside parking lot. Instead use the pull off at the end of the off ramp. You can shorten the approach a couple minutes by watching for a well tramped track going uphill just a few metres after the gate which cuts out the F…

reports.title: Big V - Healy Creek
reports.comment: quick: Skipped the gigantic gondola line at SSV and went up Healy creek. Absolutely nobody to be seen throughout the day! There's a track going up Healy ridge line and up Y drainage. We scoped Big V and dug a pit at 2400m - HS165cm. Got CT27 SP down on the Dec layer, but ECTN. Big V also ran almost to the skin track during the last big cycle, and was untracked (until today at least). Really good c…

reports.title: Sunshine Backcountry
reports.comment: quick: Amazing snow right now off the SE face of mt Standish and the east aspect off twin Cairns.  Surface hoar was growing over night. Height of snow was 160 cm.  Our compression test was giving moderate (RP) results on a windslap on suncrust at 100cm on SE aspect at 2350m.  No wind and lots of Sun but not quite warm enough for a suncrust to form.

reports.title: Healy alpine SSV
reports.comment: quick: Toured from top of Standish - high winds had us bail on our Twin Cairns traverse. We decided to check out some chutes we had noticed to skier’s left of the Dinosaure Head area and across from Y drainage. Ski cut some slab near the entrance of the chute we nicknamed Slabby’s Not Happy, which quickly caused a Sz1 loose dry to run the length of the chute (which we were expecting). Skied down t…

reports.title: Spray River Falls Ice Climbing
reports.comment: quick: Ice climbed Spray River Falls and followed the fresh tracks of another party on supportive and good snow in the gully. No reactivity or wind slabs encountered.

reports.comment: snowpack: No repeatable result, irregular collapse at the bottom on CT

reports.title: Sunshine Backcountry - variable results on persistent layers
reports.comment: snowpack: Test result from a few days ago shows the Dec 13th facet/surface hoar layer, down 70 cm, was found to be reactive on a protected NE aspect.  Meanwhile, at a similar elevation on a nearby SW aspect and in the sunshine snow study plot it was not reactive.  The current weak layers are spotty in distribution and it's worthwhile to dig down to test the layers before committing to the slope. C…

reports.title: Big whoompfs and CTE2
reports.comment: quick: Original objective was across the highway on the SW side but about 3 or 4 other groups had the same objective at the same time and we didn’t like the idea of skiing with several other groups around, especially given some references in the avy bulletin about potential for skier triggering etc that suggested something spooky is showing up occasionally in the snowpack.  Decided to turn back, c…

reports.title: Ice - Radioactive Beagle
reports.comment:
quick: Approach:
More hill than it looks. A travelled trail is established to follow although can be a little rough in spots. The track initially go up to an unnamed short steep flow. Said to be W4 but short. To get to Radioactive Beagle, looks for tracks that traverse over. We went to the unnamed W4 first then came down and over to RB. Our descent came directly downhill and I have to wonder if go…

reports.title: Quartz ridge tour
reports.comment:
quick: Toured over to the first bump of quartz ridge. Ski penetration was about 10-20 cm in the meadows. The ridge was very wind affected. Skiing down to leeward side had about 20-30 cm of snow on a hard crust. Skiing quality was much better closer to rock isle lake (again on leeward side). 
No signs of instabilities through the day. 
Wind was gusty and from the south/southwest.

reports.title: Wawa
reports.comment:
quick: Dug a quick pit on the Wawa face before skiing it. I knew the area slid on Jan 4th, but wanted to see what it looked like. Very wind affected area but consolidated.
145cm depth, snow was heavy and well bonded. Sugary/facet snow near ground level. 2 column tests revealed no results. It's pretty solid up there, at least the place we dug, snow was ok, still better than a day at work.

reports.title: Radioactive Beagle ice climb
reports.comment: quick: Crust on facets plus not finding the main trail made the approach a little tough. Climb is mostly snice at this point, but still in. We added a rock anchor to replace the pins.

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: We took a quiet day to check out the Healy pass area. Coming out of the tree line at the pass we skied the first ridge on the right. We were content to stop at about 2325m, or about 100m from the ridge proper and begin descending. Above the tree line the snow became slightly heavier but still fairly loose lose powder, with no noticeable crust on top. The sun peeked through the clouds for a …

reports.title: Sunshine Ski Area Snow Profile
reports.comment: quick: Profile at Sunshine ski area study plot (2200m).

reports.title: Sunshine Backcountry
reports.comment: quick: All aspects in the alpine were wind hammered and very poor skiing. At treeline some good turns on protected south aspects but mostly poor.  Below treeline we found a lot of good snow.

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment:
quick: Snow was VERY wind affected! Very hard on all aspects. Some wind loading noted, but the snow was all very firm, styrofoamy.  There were a few turns to be had, in-between sliding on hard wind hammered snow, and popping through a wind crust.

Good thing it was sunny and beautiful!

reports.title: Wizard chutes
reports.comment: quick: No instability’s notes other than the faceted loose surface snow causing some big sluffing. Surprisingly great skiing!

reports.title: Wawa ridge
reports.comment:
quick: 10-15cm of fresh powder covered a crust on the ridge, extra caution was taken when traveling in steeper terrain. 

The snow pack below was observed to be stable and well packed.

Main concern was sloughing of the powder in the alpine.

reports.title: Sunshine Slack Country
reports.comment: snowpack: CT m4 45cm planer on  30 degree slope. Skiing was very good and no other instabilities were witnessed around Twin Cairns and Rock isle lake areas.

reports.title: Helicopter Avalanche Control for Sunshine Road - Bourgeau Paths
reports.comment: avalanche: Helicopter Avalanche control on Mt. Bourgeau Paths; 4 size 1.5 slab avalanches triggered in the alpine with crowns up to 30 deep and 40 m wide. 4 shots with no result.

reports.title: Sunshine Road Avalanche Control - Eagle 3 pahts
reports.comment: avalanche: Helicopter Explosive control on Eagle 3 paths: 2 x 12.5 kg explosives triggered thin (10 cm thick) windslabs, size 1 from the alpine start zone.

reports.title: SSV Meadows Full Profile
reports.comment: quick: Went out to the Meadows today to do a full profile practice. ECTX and CTN, Pretty positive resistant snow pack￼ for all the facets ￼, ￼ see photo for all the details ￼

reports.comment: avalanche: Skiing resort and slack country at Sunshine.  Saw this debris field on the third day from the summit on Lookout Mountain.

reports.title: deep cory pass
reports.comment: quick: The skiing here was almost too good to be true. wouldn’t recommend this spot if conditions are worse than yellow yellow red because of overhead, but everything was settled nicely and snowpack was very well consolidated. We had very little wind activity where we were, but there were a few sluffs of snow being blown around near the mountain top, with nothing triggering. There were a couple of…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing in the trees at Healy Pass. Maybe 5cm of fresh snow. Open areas quite wind affected.
Pretty warm temperatures all day, wind was really picking up at about 2pm.

reports.title: Healy Creek Avalanche Paths
reports.comment: quick: On our return back down Healy Creek, we saw new avalanche debris on SE facing slide paths. It appears that the cornice above failed and triggered a wind slab directly below which propagated and ran down the central avalanche path and in addition, it spread to the lookers right path and stepped down to a deeper layer over a convex roll and ran mid-path. Estimating Size 3 if considered as one…

reports.title: Sulphur mt, waterfall drainage area
reports.comment: quick: Cheeky walk along the ridge to scout lines.  Aware of the forecast and thoughtful of the hazard to potential trail walkers below.  Ridgewalk produced red flags: drum like + hollow noises, cracks and signs of slabbing over a weak layer, and collapsing faceted snow.  Verbalizing the likehood of turning around.  Hopeful that instabilities were localized to the windy ridgetop, continued to a 's…

reports.title: Bourgeau Left Hand Natural Size 3.5
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed by skiiers downloading Sunshine Village gondola around 5pm. Photo from Parks Canada overflight on Feb. 24th, 2021. Avalanche ran over ice climb and the powder cloud dusted cars in the parking lot.

reports.title: Healy pass trail Colum test
reports.comment:
avalanche: Saw avalanche debris on South face near the start of the Healy pass trail from the sunshine resorts parking / snowpack: Colum test
Fracture reaction Helbow 2 at 20/25 in. 
No propagation on propagation test

reports.title: Pilot Paths
reports.comment: avalanche: All but one of the east aspect Pilot paths avalanched in the past few days. There was a dusting of new snow found over the debris. A couple of the paths went full runout, others stopped short. A couple of bed sections were showing ground. Didn't have time to collect other info and vis wasn't great from below due to cloud cover. Avalanche date/time is simply a guess.

reports.title: Sunshine Slack Country
reports.comment: snowpack: Skied laps on N/NE slopes in Rock isle Lake area. All other slopes were wind affected.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge
reports.comment: quick: We went up Wawa Ridge in a white-out, sticking to the ridge which had little snow on it due to wind.  At the top, the sun came out and we skied down a 30 degree slope that had 10 cm of new snow on it.  There was a hard wind crust beneath and it felt solid.  Our ECT test showed a little fracturing 40cm down, but no propagation (taken on a wind loaded 25 degree slope (SE Aspect). / snowpack: …

reports.title: SSV / Quartz
reports.comment: quick: Toured in the SSV slack - objective was Quartz 2 but we ended up going down the col between 1 and 2 due to lack of viz, strong winds, etc. Quartz 2 did look really good (when we saw it). Lots of wind effect up Quartz 1, building gigantic cornices (at the usual spot). Had mabybe 5-10cm of unconsolidated on top of buried wind slab which was non reactive. Good turns were had but we kept it sup…

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment: quick: Climbed Spray River Falls, good travel up the drainage on avalanche debris releasing from south/south-east facing rock on previous days. Strong melt-freeze cycle created planar ice and interesting conditions (thin brittle skin on some areas). Sun only affected the drainage and climb for a short time in the morning and had firmed up again by the time we descended (around 3:30pm).

reports.title: Spray River Falls
reports.comment: quick: Got to the base of the climb around 1pm and waited for the sun to go over the mountains.  The sun was not hitting the approach slopes much that day (except for maybe a minute as we neared the base of the climb).  Approach slopes felt stable but definitely enough snow to trigger a large slab avalanche.  Evidence of old avalanche debris at the base of the climb.  When rappelling down the firs…

reports.title: Ball range conditions
reports.comment:
quick: Healy pass/Egypt lake/shadow lake

Skiing:Alpine was wind hammered on all aspects, poor skiing. Best skiing found in sheltered terrain on all aspects in the trees, temp crusts quickly turned into moist surface snow below 1900m.

Weather: Was extremely windy over the 3 days with steady strong SW winds and very strong gusts. Winds and warmth seemed to have spiked natural activity over wed to …

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Sunny but fairly cool day at Healy Pass April 13. Air temperature stayed around zero all day. Trail from Sunshine is in excellent condition. Good skiing on E and N aspects in the alpine, some sun effect on south slopes.
Column test at 2500m elevation, 1:00pm
Monarch Ramparts. ENE aspect 300m south of Healy Pass.
HS 290cm HSS 23cm
CT Easy SP 5 at 23 cm. Not sure if the interface is sun or wi…

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: quick: Good freeze with easy travel conditions.  Some skate skiers made it to citadel pass.  It started out sunny then clouded over at 1130.  We skied the east aspect off of quartz hill but it was not quite soft at 1130.  Found some good corn skiing on mellow south facing slopes above howard douglas lake.  The snow  was very supportive and  the skinning was fast and easy back to the resort at 230.…

reports.title: Citadel Peak
reports.comment: quick: Climbied citadel peak via the lower angled south ridge.  The east ridge was too soft by the time I got there around noon. Good travel early in the morning but the over night freeze below 2400m was pretty weak. Wind exposed slopes froze better.  Sank a few times through the crust especially in treed areas around 2250m after 11 am.  A few cms fell by convective flurries around 4pm.  Skin wax …

reports.title: Twin Cairns
reports.comment:
quick: Spent the last three days skiing around sunshine.

Wednesday I skied the north and west aspects off of Twin Cairns.  Great dust on crust conditions and a great freeze.  Circled back out via the Healy pass trail.  The trail is covered in tree litter and looked disgusting but travel supportive and not too sticky at 1 pm.  It has seen some hikers and would not recommend it and that's before th…

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: quick: There was a skiable freeze above 2200m in the sunshine Meadows. Steep east and south alpine aspects were wet at 9am and avalanche activity began on these aspects at 930am.  The travel and ski conditions were still good when I when inbounds at 130pm but the crust felt like it was about to get punchy. Looks like a mild freeze tonight in the Alpine with hotter weather.  A ton of avalanche acti…

reports.title: Bourgeau - size 3 ?
reports.comment: quick: Lazy day at the resort today - but upon returning to parking at 2pm, heard (and then saw) that Bourgeau was shedding over the ice fall route. Must’ve lasted like 3min and it looked almost like Takakkaw Falls - huge volume of snow came down. Didn’t see start zone but suspect a lot of the face ripped off.
